structured_output.summary: a41fd4a resolves the three reproduced defects on the paths I traced: parent-loss cleanup under ps failure (lib/_docguardian.py:182-194 now SIGKILLs unconditionally while the direct child is unreaped), pending SIGINT handoff (outer defer spans spawn/pin construction, handles assigned before unblock, pin construction moved inside try at :240), and original signal mask through nested deferral (explicit signal_mask threaded to GroupPin and spawn_in_group). No destructive group signal follows pin-release or direct-child reap on the traced paths. One conditional gap remains: the pre-spawn exception path SIGKILLs a PGID with no ownership anchor, so parent loss plus pin exit can hit a reused PGID. Minor gaps: post-reap probe failure, deadline overrun in cleanup, and no structured handling at the _docexamples boundary. Evidence is local macOS/static only; no both-platform acceptance and SPEC rev 7 and test_group_pin.py were not read. Conclusions are from static reading and no tests were run.

findings.title: Pre-spawn exception path can SIGKILL a reused PGID after parent loss and pin exit
findings.body: When process is None the handler does os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL) with no ownership anchor. The pin exits by itself on parent loss when no startup-release exists (_docgroup_pin.py:156-159) and init then reaps it, freeing the PGID once the group is empty. A guardian exception in that window (read/atomic/ps/MemoryError) signals a PGID that may belong to an unrelated group. This is the previously unconfirmed parent-loss plus independent pin death/reuse concern; it holds only on this pre-spawn branch, since the post-spawn branch is anchored by the unreaped workload child. Inferred from code, not reproduced; narrow window.
findings.recommendation: Drop the pre-spawn killpg (no workload exists before startup-release) or verify the pin is still a live/zombie unreaped child before signalling. Add a test for a pre-spawn exception with the pin already gone.

findings.title: Post-reap probe failure leaves no group cleanup when parent is also gone
findings.body: A ps failure at :165 after direct_child_reaped is True goes to the handler, which skips the kill because the child is reaped. A straggler that joined the group between the :152 check and the reap survives if the parent is gone; the parent-side pin SIGKILL at :281-285 only helps while the parent lives. Terminal state is reported as guardian-failure/cleanup-unverified, so it is not silent.
findings.recommendation: Issue the group SIGKILL before the direct-child reap decision, or keep the pin-anchored kill before release regardless of the reaped flag. Test a single post-reap probe failure.

findings.title: Cleanup waits can overrun the absolute deadline; SIGINT blocked during pin-ready poll
findings.body: The pin readiness loop runs inside run()'s outer defer so SIGINT/SIGTERM stay blocked up to 5s (bounded by ready_deadline). On timeout finish() adds up to 3s and the handler's process.wait(5) adds more; the deadline is only checked at loop heads. Bounded but nonzero overrun. SPEC rev 7 tolerance not verified.
findings.recommendation: Confirm against SPEC rev 7 deadline contract; narrow the blocked region to Popen only and cap cleanup waits to the remaining budget.

findings.title: No structured handling of guardian.run exceptions at the production boundary
findings.body: guardian.run is called without try/except. Launcher, atomic or KeyboardInterrupt exceptions propagate after run()'s finally cleanup, but the TemporaryDirectory removes terminal.json including cleanup_error/cleanup-unverified evidence. Cleanup claim holds; observability is lost.
findings.recommendation: Catch Exception around guardian.run, record a guardian-failure lifecycle in stage provenance, and re-raise KeyboardInterrupt after recording.

findings.title: Test coverage gaps for new repairs
findings.body: The probe-failure test makes every ps call fail so it never exercises a single post-reap failure. The pending-SIGINT test is in-process with parent_pid=getppid(), so it does not cover real parent loss with pending SIGINT. No test covers pre-spawn killpg reuse or independent pin death. Evidence is Darwin ps path only; the waitid branch and Linux/Python 3.15 CI are not exercised locally.
findings.recommendation: Add tests for the pin-gone pre-spawn exception and single post-reap probe failure, and obtain Linux and macOS CI acceptance.
